name: Nick Kurtz
assessment: Kurtz has 50 A/AA PA, four HR, twelve walks and ten K at age 21. His .63 preseason rank and draft pick are present, not missing. Adding earlier rows lowers arrival 6.06% to 3.87% despite conditional PA rising 168 to 176; expected PA falls 10.18 to 6.81 against 489. Rank contributes positively in both saved classifiers, but its path effect weakens, along with other refitted paths. Broad active support rises 15 to 20, while refined elite-thin active support remains zero. Earlier and current nearest strict level peers mostly lack equivalent elite pedigree and cannot explain away the miss. Rate improves -.063 to .041 but remains far below observed 5.150 custom batting wins/600. This is an unresolved readiness and talent miss, not evidence that his productive short sample was absent.

name: Wyatt Langford
assessment: Langford's 200 PA include 54 AA and 26 AAA, with ten HR, 36 walks and 34 K, age 21 and .95 rank. Dominant A-plus is a review label; every level count reaches the model. Expected PA falls 214.92 to 163.97: arrival falls 59.91% to 51.07%, active workload 358.74 to 321.10. In the conditional tree rank's positive path declines 147.25 to 128.29 PA and the zero-MLB-work path becomes more negative. Rate rises .688 to .823, away from actual .549, so neither change improves the forecast against 557 PA. Refined active support remains zero; early Belt is a relevant split-exposure example, but ordinary unranked strict peers are not equivalent college fast tracks. No missing-input bug or causal team explanation was established.

name: Pete Alonso
assessment: Alonso has 574 AA/AAA PA, 36 HR, 73 walks and 128 K, following two earlier professional years. His ranked .50 signal is present. Both models give roughly 80% appearance, but conditional PA drops 267.58 to 262.94, leaving expected PA 210.50 against 693. The zero-current-MLB inputs remain major negative conditional tree paths, while rank and AAA HR contribute positively. Rate .286 to .221 also moves away from observed 3.283. Broad active AAA-age support rises 48 to 60, but refined support stays seven. Thaiss, VanMeter, Mercado and Walsh provide variable arrival workloads, not proof that Alonso should be priced like an average arrival. Extra older data does not fix this established upper-minors readiness miss.

name: Ronald Acuña Jr.
assessment: Acuna's 612 A-plus/AA/AAA PA include 21 HR, 43 walks and 144 K at age 19; his .99 preseason rank is unchanged. Expected PA rises 101.53 to 172.93 through appearance 48.22% to 71.07% and conditional PA 210.55 to 243.31. New saved paths redistribute contributions across AA exposure, games and age; rank stays strongly positive, so the improvement is not a repaired rank join. One active teenage-AAA person, Jesus Montero 2010, enters this actual held fold, versus none before. Only two strict forecast peers exist. Rate barely changes .164 to .170 against 3.681, and value .340 to .581 remains below 4.145. This is a useful partial readiness gain, not sufficient superstar support or proof that Montero caused it alone.

name: Julio Rodríguez
assessment: Julio's 340 A-plus/AA PA contain thirteen HR, 42 walks and 66 K at age 20, after 2019 production and a canceled 2020 MiLB season. His 40-man listing and .98/.96 ranks are present. Expected PA falls 254.11 to 210.57, through both lower arrival and active PA. The listing remains positive in the classifier but its path effect declines; the current zero-MLB-work conditional penalty grows and prior rank lift shrinks. Rate .754 to .766 improves slightly but not nearly enough for actual 560 PA and 2.683 rate. Broad active support rises 20 to 28, refined remains nine. Iglesias/Rosario/Vitters/Chisenhall do not establish equivalence to Julio's talent. This harm contradicts a blanket claim that added older origins solve advancing prospects.

name: Jackson Holliday
assessment: Holliday has 581 PA across A through AAA, twelve HR, 99 walks and 118 K, age 19 and rank one. Arrival rises 88.68% to 90.90% and conditional PA 396.01 to 416.87, increasing expected PA 351.19 to 378.95 versus 208. Current-rank lift grows in the conditional fit while other paths offset it partly. Rate .621 to .600 is slightly closer to the observed -2.838 but remains optimistic, so value rises 1.451 to 1.552 against -.503. Some extra profile support arrives, but nine refined active people are not star-specific certification. Older Heyward 623 PA is a useful successful timing example, not a mandate for Holliday. This retains an important false-high stress case.

name: Aaron Judge
assessment: Established Judge has 696/458/704 MLB PA and 62/37/58 HR in his dated history. New expected PA 565.72 improves on 530.75 against 679, mostly through conditional workload 535.74 to 570.26, not appearance already above 99%. Saved trees use high workload, quality and PA/game; Ridge uses pooled and recent MLB quality. Rate falls 4.534 to 4.500 against actual 6.287, so value improvement 5.668 to 6.010 comes from PA and still understates 9.393 custom batting-plus-replacement wins. Numerous coarse/refined active peers do not mean adequate support for Judge-level talent. The better workload direction is sensible; the forecast remains conservative.

name: Hector Martinez
assessment: Hector Martinez is 17 with 204 DSL PA, four HR, 33 walks and 49 K after 186 DSL PA the year before. Both immediate arrival chances are about .1%, with expected PA .089 to .108 and actual zero. The extended conditional forecast rises 59 to 83 but both active and rate DSL profiles have zero training people. The positive rate .347 to .449 is mainly age/age-square and generic position effects, not validated DSL-to-MLB batting ability; actual inactive rate is null, not zero. Four origin-selected DSL peers also have zero next-year PA, which supports immediate rarity only, not a career-talent claim. No long-term prospect valuation conclusion is warranted.

name: Nelson Cruz
assessment: Cruz has three high-workload MLB seasons with 43/39/37 HR at age 37. Appearance rises 61.83% to 75.24%, conditional PA stays about 443/447, and expected PA rises 274.09 to 336.18 versus 521. The original soft nonlisting is a negative classifier path; the refitted model redistributes listing, games, workload and age effects. This branch lacks complete preseason employment/contract information, so a soft nonlisting must not be read as known unavailability. Rate rises 1.683 to 1.808 versus 4.779, increasing value 1.613 to 2.048 versus 6.260. This largest value gain is still a major miss; Thome/Ibanez and the retired or low-workload older peers show uncertainty, not a causal signing forecast.

name: José Bautista
assessment: Bautista's 673/666/517 MLB PA and 35/40/22 HR show productive but declining recent production at age 35. Appearance 53.70% to 89.45% and expected PA 270.48 to 455.45 improve strongly toward 686 actual, with conditional PA nearly unchanged. Saved classifier paths change on recent games, prior workload and soft nonlisting. Yet rate stays 2.277/2.307 versus -1.223 actual; the higher PA magnifies that optimistic yield, worsening value 1.861 to 3.157 against .979. This is the largest value harm, but it is not a failed playing-time forecast direction. Nor does it prove independent-means multiplication is inherently wrong: finite talent and workload fits can interact badly even with PA-weighted rate estimation.

name: Chris Davis
assessment: Davis's 47/38/26 HR and 670/665/524 MLB PA accompany rising strikeout rates and reduced recent quality. Both models correctly give high appearance and roughly 500 PA; extended expected PA 481.22 versus actual 522 is slightly worse than 502.67. Rate remains 1.08 versus -3.68 actual, producing value +2.345 against -1.963: the largest false high is overwhelmingly a talent-collapse miss, not an arrival problem. Ridge still assigns positive effects to pooled quality and multiple workload terms; the saved models do not add a cliff-collapse state. An unforeseen collapse and a potentially overpersistent representation are separate explanations; this comparison alone cannot decide how predictable the full collapse was.

name: Aaron Judge
assessment: Debut-year Judge has 410 AAA PA with nineteen HR, 47 walks and 98 K, plus 95 MLB PA with four HR and 42 K. High appearance is already sensible, but conditional PA falls 335.05 to 317.43, so expected PA drops 309.92 to 296.78 versus 678 actual. Rank stays positive while the low-current-MLB conditional penalty grows. Rate rises -.040 to .018 but misses the 5.330 breakout; value .936 to .924 remains far below 8.372. Refined support remains one despite many broad debut/AAA people. Renfroe and Moreland demonstrate possible workloads, not that all such hitters become Judge. Both workload and breakout-talent uncertainty remain; more source rows did not solve them.

name: Travis Demeritte
assessment: Demeritte's 494 AA PA, seventeen HR, 56 walks and 140 K follow 511 AA and 530 A-plus PA. Arrival drops 9.42% to 6.28% and conditional PA 96.99 to 89.88; expected PA 9.14 to 5.65 is very wrong versus 186. Rate -.325 to -.397 also remains too optimistic versus -2.379. Nevertheless value .0232 to .0137 nearly matches .0157 actual. He was selected as ordinary by delivered-value error, but the walkthrough proves he is not well predicted on the components: low predicted exposure accidentally compensates for poor hitting. Zero-PA peers Call/Raley/Alvarez/Rooker do not establish the focal player's correct arrival probability. This case warns against certifying models from value alone.

name: Cody Bellinger
assessment: Bellinger has 465 AA PA plus twelve AAA PA with 26 combined HR, 58 walks and 94 K at age 20, after thirty A-plus HR. He is ranked .88 and all split-level counts are present. Expected PA falls 102.57 to 45.75: arrival 39.90% to 25.71% and conditional PA 257.04 to 177.94 both worsen against 548 actual. Conditional paths show a stronger zero-current-MLB penalty and unfavorable tiny-AAA PA/game path; rank remains positive. Rate .085 to .066 also misses 2.700, making value .331 to .146 versus 4.365. Broad support improves, refined active stays five. Moustakas 365 PA and Mesoraco 53 illustrate different timing, not justification for this large harm. This is the largest prospect deterioration and blocks a blanket promotion.
